Each stage saves and the standard native driver performs two separate cold reloads. Source setup disables only the exact original disposable fixture lab before starting its own lab. The test never assigns selected paid levels, writes recipe productivity or accesses MIR storage. It changes only its own recipe/lab, Tin cap defaults and fixed hundred-pack timing for two selected tails. The controlled return is not a claim about a real mod's Tin recipe.

Readmission appends Tin after the eligible current Automation research without replacing its queue or progress. Its owned lab refills only the remaining part of a finite400-pack budget as native inventory slots permit, observes one legitimate Automation completion and then requires three Tin completions. The original one-shot400-pack insertion failed on actual slot capacity and remains a separate failed fixture result.

The original literal-current/queue observer caught the actual42% to43% progression while both disabled flags were false. Independent policy reviewAF40D52D identifies native cap-style cancellation with saved work as the correct boundary; requiring disabled Bronze to remain current is incompatible with stopping its lab. The corrected mode-specific observer still rejects that broken behavior and preserves every original failed result under its original identity. Native remainder and saved-progress preservation must be observed; an API description does not supply their pass.

Materialize each stage wrapper together with the two shared Lua modules as one fixture ZIP. The three existing native-driver calls use protected copies of the previous stage's exact save, matching profiles and exact archive hashes; preserve every original result. Host controls exercise opposing loss/reset/queue/admission cases but are not native acceptance. Physical Tin output, ordinary research tuning, arbitrary provider changes, multiplayer and performance remain outside this fixture.
